question: The term 'License Raj' is related to which sector of the Indian economy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term '**License Raj**' refers to the elaborate system of licenses, regulations, and red tape required to set up and run businesses in India, primarily affecting the **industrial sector**.
 
• It was introduced after India gained independence in 1947 as part of the country's planned economic development strategy under a socialist framework.
 
• The License Raj system required businesses to seek approvals from multiple government agencies before starting new projects or expanding existing operations.
 
• The system was characterized by excessive bureaucratic interference, which often led to inefficiency and corruption in the industrial sector.
 
• The License Raj was significantly dismantled during the economic reforms initiated in **1991**, which aimed to liberalize the Indian economy and reduce government control over industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991:**

 
 
• The reforms were introduced by the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao and then Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
 
• They aimed to liberalize the Indian economy by reducing tariffs, deregulating markets, and opening up the economy to foreign investments.
 
• The policy marked a significant departure from the License Raj system, allowing industries to grow with fewer restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of License Raj on Industry:**
 
 
• Discouraged entrepreneurship and innovation due to excessive bureaucratic control.
 
• Led to inefficiencies and delays in industrial projects.
 
• Encouraged corruption as businesses often had to bribe officials to obtain licenses.
 
 
 
• **Post-1991 Industrial Growth:**
 
 
• The economic reforms led to the liberalization of the industrial sector, resulting in increased foreign investments.
 
• Industries experienced greater autonomy and growth due to the reduction of restrictive regulations.
 
 
 
• **Globalization and the Indian Economy:**
 
 
• Globalization post-1991 enabled Indian industries to compete in the global market.
 
• It facilitated the growth of sectors such as information technology and manufacturing.
